title: Close the DNS-rebinding window in LiveFetcher
objective: Make the LiveFetcher connection provably reach an address that passed the SSRF policy, closing the time-of-check/time-of-use window between the validation DNS lookup and urllib's independent connect-time lookup, without weakening any existing control and without moving TLS certificate verification off the hostname.
defect: LiveFetcher.fetch called _resolve(host) and vetted the returned addresses, then handed the URL to urllib, which performed its own DNS resolution at TCP connect. The vetted address was therefore not necessarily the connected address. Raised as residual R1 by a Level-2 evaluator on PR #14 and correctly judged not a gate for that slice: LiveFetcher is off by default and a per-hop SSRF recheck exists, so this is defence in depth, not a live exploit.
approach: A: resolve once per hop, require every returned address to pass, and dial the validated address literals rather than the hostname, so no second name lookup remains to rebind.
B: re-check the socket's real peer with getpeername() inside the connection hook, before the TLS handshake and before any request byte is written.
Both, at one seam: http.client's per-instance _create_connection is replaced, so self.host keeps the hostname and the Host header, TLS SNI and certificate hostname verification are untouched.
out_of_scope_zero_diff: apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/** (a concurrent slice owns the provider adapters and fixtures)
every manifest, lockfile, dependency override and audit configuration
promotion or merge of the draft pull request
acceptance_criteria: A1: A resolver stub answering the validation lookup with a public address and the connect-time lookup with a private address reaches the private address on base and is refused after the change.
A2: That regression test genuinely fails on the unmodified tree, and a positive control proves the harness can observe a connection to a blocked address at all.

A3: Loopback, RFC1918, link-local including 169.254.169.254, the unspecified address, IPv6 loopback/link-local/ULA, IPv4-mapped forms including ::ffff:127.0.0.1, multicast and reserved addresses are all refused.
A4: A host resolving to a mix of safe and unsafe addresses fails closed rather than opportunistically using the safe one.
A5: The allowlist, address and peer checks re-run on every redirect hop, and each hop is pinned to the addresses that hop validated.
A6: TLS certificate verification still validates against the URL hostname, not the pinned address, and SNI is preserved on a context that keeps check_hostname on and verify_mode at CERT_REQUIRED.
A7: Address classification is not duplicated: the pre-connect check and the peer re-check both call address_block_reason.
A8: No new runtime dependency, no new mandatory service, and no platform-specific socket behaviour.
A9: The opener still omits the redirect handler, the error processor and the proxy handler.
A10: The full suite passes, no test performs external network egress, and the diff is limited to approved files with progress.md a strict base-prefix append ending in LF.
verification_plan: Reproduce the defect against the unmodified module with a standalone probe before writing the fix.
Run the final test module against base fetch.py and record which tests are red.
Run the full suite locally with and without a database, using an ephemeral PostgreSQL 16 container matching CI.
Confirm zero diff against the protected paths and a byte-identical feature ledger.
Commit, push, open a draft pull request at the first pushed commit, and inspect CI.
negative_tests: A pinned connection must not verify a certificate against the dialled IP: a certificate naming only the hostname, with no IP SAN, must still validate.
A certificate for a different hostname must still be rejected, so the positive TLS result is not an artefact of verification being off.
An unparseable or unreadable socket peer must be refused rather than allowed.
A host that resolves to nothing must be refused.
data_implications: None. No persisted row, migration, CHECK constraint, fixture or provider classification changes in this slice.
security_privacy: Security hardening only. No new logging is added, so no resolved internal address becomes an information leak; the existing typed exception messages are unchanged in shape. No secret is introduced: the optional end-to-end TLS test generates a throwaway key into a pytest temporary directory that is never committed.
portability: Standard library only (http.client, ssl, socket, urllib). No new dependency, no new service, no Linux-only socket behaviour, and amd64/arm64 unaffected.
z0_risk: No runtime Z0 change. LiveFetcher remains disabled by default and no classifier, publication or catalogue behaviour is touched.
known_ci_exception: The Dependency audit check is red on advisory GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (nanoid <3.3.18) on current origin/main as well, through no code change, because npm audit queries the live advisory database. It is an accepted, documented risk owned elsewhere. No manifest, lockfile, override or audit configuration is changed here.
